about: SOLA Devotional Plans | Bible & Theology, organized into chapters. Each plan has the months in which it is offered ("months"). The themes are renewed each month; those who have already started a plan continue with it until it ends.

plans.title: Patriarchs
plans.subtitle: Ordinary men, a faithful God
plans.intro: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph were not marble heroes. They lied, hesitated, fought within their families. Their story is, at its core, the story of God's patience with people like us.

chapters.title: Abraham: the call to the unknown

days.title: Leave your land
days.meditation: God called Abram without handing over the map. He said "go," but didn't say where. Most of us want the complete roadmap before the first step. Faith, however, almost always works like car headlights on a road at night: it lights up just a few meters, enough to keep walking. Abram left at seventy-five years old. It's never too late to start obeying.
questions: What step is God asking you to take without seeing the whole path?
Which "familiar land" do you have difficulty leaving behind?
days.application: Write in one sentence the next step of obedience you know you need to take, even without seeing the rest.

days.title: God will provide
days.meditation: Isaac's question cuts the heart: "Where is the lamb?" Abraham answers with a phrase he himself did not fully understand: "God will provide." There are moments when faith has no explanation, only trust. And the definitive answer came centuries later, on another mountain, when God Himself gave the Lamb.
questions: What might God be asking you to put on the altar?
Can you say "God will provide" before seeing the provision?
days.application: Give today, in prayer, what you most fear losing, and say out loud: "God will provide."

chapters.title: Isaac: the son of the promise

days.title: The wells reopened
days.meditation: Isaac was not a pioneer like his father. He reopened the wells that Abraham had dug. It may not seem heroic, but there is courage in caring for what we receive. When the neighbors fought over water, he did not fight; he dug another well. Sometimes victory is not in winning the argument, but in moving forward until we find space.
questions: What "wells" of faith inherited from other generations need to be reopened in your life?
In which conflict do you need to stop fighting and digging elsewhere?
days.application: Thank God today for a person who dug wells of faith before you, and, if you can, tell them so.

days.title: Meditating in the countryside
days.meditation: Isaac went out to the field at dusk to meditate. The Bible keeps this simple scene: a man alone, thinking before God. It was there, at that unhurried moment, that he looked up and saw the answer to a prayer arrive. We live so busy that there is hardly any dusk left. And maybe we are missing exactly what God is bringing along the way.
questions: When was the last time you stopped without hurry before God?
What could be coming along the road while you're too distracted to see?
days.application: Set aside ten minutes today, without a cell phone, to walk or sit silently before God.

days.title: God was in this place
days.meditation: Jacob ran away from home after deceiving his father and brother. He slept with a pillow stone and woke up saying, "The Lord is in this place, and I did not know." God does not expect us to be in good condition to appear. He visits fugitives. The loneliest place of your life may be the gate of heaven.
questions: In what difficult place can God be present without you realizing it?
What does it change to know that God met Jacob in the middle of the flight?
days.application: Look at the hardest place of your week and write: "God is here."

days.title: I won't let you go
days.meditation: Jacob spent his life fighting against everyone: his brother, his father-in-law, circumstances. That night, he fought with God. He left limping and with a new name. God sometimes defeats us to bless us. Jacob's limp was the mark that he no longer walked by his own strength alone.
questions: Against what, or against whom, have you been fighting with your own strength?
What "lameness" in your story could be a mark of an encounter with God?
days.application: Tell God sincerely where you are struggling, and ask for a blessing, not just a victory.

chapters.title: Joseph: from the well to the palace

days.title: The Lord was with Joseph
days.meditation: Joseph was sold by his brothers and became a slave in a strange land. And yet, the text repeats: "The Lord was with Joseph." It does not say that his life became easy. It says he was not alone. God's presence does not take us out of all wells, but transforms what happens inside them.
questions: Have you measured God's presence by the comfort of circumstances?
How can you be faithful in the "Egypt" you are in now?
days.application: Do your work today with excellence, like Joseph, remembering that God is with you there.

days.title: God made him good
days.meditation: After years, Joseph had the power to take revenge. He chose to forgive and said one of the Bible's deepest phrases: "You planned evil; God has turned it into good." He did not call evil good. He only recognized that God is greater than evil. That is theology learned through suffering, not in the classroom.
questions: What evil in your story have you still not delivered for God to transform?
Is there someone you need to free with your forgiveness?
days.application: Pray for the name of someone who hurt you, asking God to turn that pain into good.

plans.title: Heroes of Faith
plans.subtitle: The gallery of Hebrews 11
plans.intro: Hebrews 11 is a gallery of imperfect people who trusted in a perfect God. None of them saw everything fulfilled. All saw enough to continue.

days.title: The certainty of the invisible
days.meditation: Faith is not positive thinking nor religious optimism. It is trust supported by God's character. No one sees the wind, but everyone sees the trees moving. Faith is like this: it does not see God directly, but recognizes the marks of His action and decides to rely on Him.
questions: Is your faith supported by God's character or favorable circumstances?
Which "moving trees" show God's action in your life?
days.application: Note three pieces of evidence of God's faithfulness in your recent history.

days.title: Without faith it is impossible
days.meditation: The verse is strong: without faith it is impossible to please God. Not because God requires a minimum level of enthusiasm, but because faith is essentially trusting that He is who He says He is. A child who does not trust the father may obey out of fear, but will have no intimacy. God wants children who come closer.
questions: Do you approach God out of trust or obligation?
What does it mean, in practice, to seek God this week?
days.application: Begin your prayer today by telling God who He is for you before asking for anything.

days.title: Abel still speaks
days.meditation: Abel died young and left no recorded word. Even so, the text says he still speaks. A life of faith continues preaching after it ends. We are all leaving some kind of echo. The question is: what will your life say when you are no longer here to explain?
questions: What message would your life be preaching if it ended today?
Who spoke to your heart by faith, even after you departed?
days.application: Write a sentence about the legacy of faith you want to leave.

days.title: Noah built without seeing rain
days.meditation: Noah built a giant boat where it had never rained like that before. Imagine the neighbors' comments. Faith sometimes seems ridiculous to those who look from the outside. Noah did not have public approval, he had the word of God. And that was enough to hammer for many years.
questions: What obedience of yours seems strange to others?
Have you let other people's opinions define what you will do for God?
days.application: Take today a step of obedience that you have been avoiding out of fear of what others might think.

days.title: Moses chose
days.meditation: Moses had the palace, education, and future guaranteed. He chose to suffer with God's people. Faith is not just about believing; it is choosing. Every choice has a price, and so does every refusal. Moses looked beyond what he saw and considered that Christ was worth more than all the treasures of Egypt.
questions: What "treasure of Egypt" does your heart contend with with Christ?
What difficult choice are you putting off?
days.application: Identify a concrete choice this week in which you will place Christ above comfort.

days.title: Rahab, the Unlikely
days.meditation: Among patriarchs and prophets appears Rahab, a foreign woman with a complicated past. She is in the gallery of faith and in Jesus' genealogy. God does not have a list of ideal candidates. He has a grace that reaches the unlikely. If Rahab is there, no one is too far away.
questions: Have you ever considered yourself too unlikely for God to use?
Who have you dismissed as "unlikely" and whom God can reach?
days.application: Pray today for someone you think is too far from God.

days.title: Strengthened weak
days.meditation: Gideon was fearful, Samson was impulsive, David fell badly. Still, they are on the list. The text says that strength was drawn from weakness. The heroes of faith were not strong who became stronger; they were weak who leaned on God. This is good news for all of us.
questions: What weakness could your God use if you gave it to Him?
Have you been waiting to get strong before serving?
days.application: Tell God, honestly, the weakness that shames you most, and ask for His strength.

days.title: Looking at Jesus
days.meditation: After the gallery, the author puts us on the track. The cloud of witnesses is not there to judge us, but to encourage us. And the center of it all is not any hero, it is Jesus, the author and finisher of faith. Runners who look back stumble. Runners who look toward the arrival continue.
questions: What weight do you need to lose to run better?
Where have your eyes been fixed lately?
days.application: Choose a concrete weight (a habit, a resentment) and surrender it to God today.

plans.title: Apostles
plans.subtitle: Called, formed, and sent
plans.intro: Fishermen, a tax collector, a skeptic, and a persecutor. Jesus did not choose the most prepared; He prepared those He chose.

days.title: Get away from me
days.meditation: After the miraculous catch, Peter does not celebrate. He falls to his knees: "Depart from me, I am a sinner." The holiness of Jesus exposed his smallness. But Jesus does not turn away; He calls. The first step of discipleship is to realize who we are before who He is.
questions: When was the last time Jesus' greatness brought him to his knees?
Which "boat" do you need to leave to follow it closer?
days.application: Start the day by acknowledging before God an area where you need His grace.

days.title: Get up and follow me
days.meditation: Matthew was a tax collector, someone the people hated. Jesus passed by the tax office and said two words: "Follow me." Matthew left the money table. How many people have we already discarded whom Jesus would call by name? And how many times do we think our past disqualifies us?
questions: What "collection table" traps you to the past?
Who have you considered unworthy of an invitation from Jesus?
days.application: Invite someone unlikely today for coffee or a conversation about faith.

days.title: Can something good come from Nazareth?
days.meditation: Nathanael was prejudiced and did not hide it. Philip did not argue; he only said: "Come and see." Sometimes, the best argument is not a thesis, it is an invitation. Jesus was not offended by Nathanael's doubt; He revealed himself to him. Honest sincerity is usually closer to faith than polite indifference.
questions: What prejudice could be preventing you from seeing something God is doing?
Have you invited people to "come and see" or just tried to win arguments?
days.application: Instead of arguing, tell someone today, simply, what Jesus did in your life.

days.title: My Lord and my God
days.meditation: Thomas was reputed to be unbelieving, but it was his one of the highest confessions in the New Testament. Jesus did not rebuke him harshly; he showed his wounded hands. Doubts, when brought to Jesus, can end in worship. The problem is not asking; it is running away with questions.
questions: What doubt have you kept away from Jesus?
What do Christ's wounds say about his questions?
days.application: Write down your greatest doubt of faith and bring it to God in prayer, without fear.

days.title: Do you love me?
days.meditation: Peter denied Jesus three times near a campfire. Jesus restores him with three questions near another campfire. He does not humiliate; he heals. And, with each answer, he returns to Peter a mission. Failure is not the end of the story of those who love Jesus; it can be the beginning of a humbler ministry.
questions: What failure do you think disqualified you from serving God?
If Jesus asked you today, "Do you love me?", what would you answer sincerely?
days.application: Answer Jesus' question in writing and think of a "sheep" you can care for this week.

days.title: They had been with Jesus
days.meditation: The authorities saw two uneducated men speaking boldly and concluded: "They were with Jesus." It wasn't the diploma that impressed, it was the mark of coexistence. No one spends time with Jesus without it appearing. The question is whether people notice this in us.
questions: What do people perceive in you that can only come from living with Jesus?
Have you spent time with him or just talked about him?
days.application: Set aside time today just to be with Jesus, reading a Gospel without hurry.

days.title: Saul, Saul
days.meditation: Saul was going to Damascus full of certainties and left blind, guided by the hand. Sometimes God needs to take away our sight so that we can see. The church's greatest persecutor became its greatest missionary. No one is beyond the reach of grace, not even those who are fighting against it.
questions: What certainty could your God be trying to tear down to show you something greater?
Who did you stop praying for because you thought you would never change?
days.application: Return to praying today for the person you consider most distant from God.

days.title: Fight the good fight
days.meditation: Paul writes about a prison, near the end. He does not talk about success, he talks about fidelity: I fought, I finished, I kept. It is a very different way of measuring life. In the end, the question will not be how much applause we receive, but whether we remain faithful until the finish line.
questions: How are you measuring the success of your life?
What would it mean for you to "keep the faith" at this stage?
days.application: Write down what you wish you could say to God at the end of your journey.

plans.title: The Greater Prophets
plans.subtitle: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Ezekiel and Daniel
plans.intro: The prophets spoke in times of crisis, exile, and silence. They spoke of judgment, but always with stubborn hope. They are ancient voices for today's weary hearts.

chapters.title: Isaiah: the vision that changes everything

days.title: Woe is me
days.meditation: In the year the king died, Isaiah saw the King who never dies. The first reaction was not enthusiasm, it was heartbreak: "Woe is me." A true vision of God always gives us a true vision of ourselves. Anyone who has never felt small before God may not have truly seen Him yet.
questions: What "king" had to fall into your life for you to see the true King?
Is your image of God big enough to break your pride?
days.application: Read Psalm 99 slowly and let God's holiness fill your prayer today.

days.title: Here I am
days.meditation: After being purified, Isaiah hears the question: "To whom shall I send it?" He does not ask where or for how long. He only says: "Here I am." Availability comes before the task description. We usually ask for the contract before signing. Isaiah signed blankly.
questions: Have you conditioned your availability on knowing all the details?
Where might God be asking, "Whom shall I send?" in your life?
days.application: Pray today: "Here I am," and stay alert for a concrete opportunity to serve.

days.title: Before I formed you
days.meditation: Jeremiah thought he was too young. God replied that He knew him before the womb. Our insecurity usually looks inward: "I can't speak," "I'm not of age." God points outward: "I am with you." Vocation does not arise from our competence, but from the presence of the one who calls.
questions: What excuse have you given God not to do what He asks?
How does knowing that God knew you before you were born change the way you see yourself?
days.application: Write your main insecurity and, next to it, the promise: "I am with you."

days.title: At the potter's house
days.meditation: The vase was ruined in the potter's hands, and he did not throw it away. He made another vase with the same clay. God does not give up the material just because the first shape did not work. Being clay is humiliating, but it is also hopeful: clay can still be shaped.
questions: What part of your life seems like a broken vase?
Are you resisting the Potter's hands or letting yourself be molded?
days.application: Give God in prayer an area of your life that you would like Him to redo.

days.title: Remember and wait
days.meditation: Lamentations is a book of mourning about a destroyed city. And, right in the midst of pain, the prophet decides to bring something to memory. His hope does not arise from the landscape, but from the remembrance of God's character. There are days when faith is this: not feeling, but remembering.
questions: What do you usually remember on bad days?
What truth about God do you need to remember today?
days.application: Memorize Lamentations 3:22-23 and repeat whenever sorrow strikes.

days.title: He does not afflict for pleasure
days.meditation: The text is delicate: God does not willingly afflict or sadden the children of men. Even discipline comes from a heart that does not take pleasure in our pain. This does not explain all suffering, but it changes the way we go through it. We are not in the hands of a cruel God, but of a Father who weeps with us.
questions: Have you seen God as someone who rejoices in your pain?
What would it be like to bring their suffering to a Father who feels compassion?
days.application: Write an honest prayer of lament, telling God what hurts, without pretending.

chapters.title: Ezekiel: a life where there were only bones

days.title: Will these bones live?
days.meditation: God takes Ezekiel to a valley of dry bones and asks: "Can these bones live?" The prophet's answer is wise: "You know it." He does not feign optimism nor give in to despair. He leaves the answer to God. And then the wind blows. No situation is too dead for the Spirit.
questions: Which area of your life looks like a valley of dry bones?
Can you answer "You know" instead of "there's no way"?
days.application: Pray today specifically for the most "dead" situation you know, asking for the breath of the Spirit.

days.title: I myself will shepherd
days.meditation: The shepherds of Israel had failed. Then God says: "I myself will tend my sheep." He seeks the lost, brings back the stray, heals the wound. It is one of the most tender prophecies of the Old Testament, fulfilled in the Good Shepherd. When leaders fail, the Shepherd does not fail.
questions: Have you been hurt by some failed human "shepherd"?
What does it mean to you that God Himself is seeking you?
days.application: Think of someone "disoriented" and take a step to reach out with a kind message.

chapters.title: Daniel: faithful in a strange land

days.title: Resolved in the heart
days.meditation: Daniel was a young exile, with a changed name and imposed culture. But he resolved in his heart not to be contaminated. Integrity does not begin in the lions' den; it begins on the lunch plate, in small decisions. Those who are faithful in little learn to be faithful when the test becomes great.
questions: What small decision today tests your loyalty?
What have you ever resolved in your heart that you will never negotiate?
days.application: Set a written integrity commitment that you will keep this week.

days.title: And, if not
days.meditation: The three friends say to the king: God can deliver us, and if not, we still will not bow. These two words, "if not," are the heart of mature faith. It does not depend on the outcome. We serve God because He is worthy, not just because He resolves. And He entered the furnace with them.
questions: Would your faith survive a "if not" from God?
What furnace are you facing, and where have you ever seen God walking with you in it?
days.application: Complete the sentence in prayer: "God can... and if not, I still will...".

plans.title: Proverbs
plans.subtitle: Wisdom for Monday
plans.intro: Proverbs is not a book for the ivory tower. It speaks of language, money, friendship, laziness, and heart. It is faith with feet on the ground of the week.

days.title: The fear of the Lord
days.meditation: Every building starts at the foundation, and wisdom begins with the fear of the Lord. Fear here is not dread, it is reverence: taking God seriously. Intelligence without reverence can build brilliant things and disastrous lives. The first step to being wise is to admit that we are not the center of the universe.
questions: In which area have you trusted your intelligence more than in God?
What would it be like to take God seriously in this week's decisions?
days.application: Before making an important decision today, stop and ask: "What honors God here?"

days.title: Trust with all your heart
days.meditation: "Do not rely on your own understanding." It does not mean turning off the brain, but not making it the last word. Our understanding is like a lantern: useful, but limited. God promises to straighten the paths of those who recognize Him on all paths, not just on Sundays.
questions: On which path have you still not recognized God?
Are you supported by your understanding or trust in it?
days.application: Surrender to God, in prayer, the decision that has occupied your mind the most.

days.title: The soft answer
days.meditation: A mild response deflects fury. Simple to understand, hard to practice. A harsh word is like gasoline in a fire. Mild is not weakness; it is strength under control. Many fights would not end in wounds if someone had chosen to lower their tone first.
questions: Who have you been responding to harshly lately?
What usually ignites your harsh word: tiredness, pride, or fear?
days.application: In the next discussion, breathe, lower your tone, and respond calmly.

days.title: Death and life
days.meditation: Language has the power of death and life. A phrase can be remembered for decades, whether as a blessing or as a wound. Words are not wind; they are seeds. The question is not only whether what we say is true, but whether it is life.
questions: What words of yours planted life or death this week?
Who needs to hear a word of life from you today?
days.application: Send someone a message of sincere encouragement today.

days.title: Keep the heart
days.meditation: From the heart come the sources of life. If the source is contaminated, everything that comes out of it will be too. We take care of the body, the house, and the car. But who takes care of the heart? Guarding the heart is watching over what enters through the eyes, ears, and thoughts we feed.
questions: What has entered your heart most often?
Which contaminated "source" do you need to close?
days.application: Choose content today that will take you out of your routine to protect your heart.

days.title: The man plans
days.meditation: The human heart charts its path, but the Lord directs its steps. Planning is good and wise. The problem is when the plan becomes a god. The safest plans are written in pencil, with the eraser in God's hands.
questions: What plan of yours are you holding on to too tightly?
Can you accept that God redirects your steps?
days.application: Write down your plans for the coming month and end with: "if the Lord wills."

days.title: Iron sharpens iron
days.meditation: Iron only sharpens iron with friction. True friendships are not only comfortable; sometimes they bother us, because they help us grow. Those who only have friends who agree with everything are going blind. God perfects us through people who love us enough to be honest.
questions: Who in your life has the freedom to say what you need to hear?
Have you been a friend who sharpens or just one who pleases?
days.application: Thank a friend today who has been honest with you, even when it hurt.

days.title: Go with the ant
days.meditation: Solomon sends the lazy man to learn from the ant. No one supervises it, but it works and prepares itself. There is a spirituality in well-done work, planning, and discipline. God does not bless laziness disguised as faith. Faith works and trusts at the same time.
questions: In which area have you been careless, waiting for something to change on its own?
How can your work be an act of worship?
days.application: Finish today a task you have been postponing, and offer it to God.

plans.title: Passion of Christ
plans.subtitle: The last days until Sunday morning
plans.intro: The Gospels dedicate a huge part to the last days of Jesus. It is no coincidence: it is there that we see up close how far God's love goes.

days.title: He cried over the city
days.meditation: In the midst of the crowd shouting hosanna, Jesus wept. He saw what the feast did not: a city that did not recognize the time of God's visit. It is possible to sing during worship and not understand who is passing by. Jesus' tears show that he is not indifferent to our blindness.
questions: Is it possible that you are celebrating Jesus without truly recognizing Him?
Who would Jesus be crying for today in your city?
days.application: Pray today for your city, naming neighborhoods and people.

days.title: Washed your feet
days.meditation: On the most important night, Jesus took a towel. The Lord of the universe knelt before dirty feet, including those of Judas. Greatness in the Kingdom is measured by the height to which we humble ourselves. None of us is above serving because he has not been.
questions: What kind of service do you consider below you?
Which "feet" would you have trouble washing?
days.application: Do a hidden and humble service today for someone in your home or work.

days.title: Don't be like me
days.meditation: In Gethsemane, Jesus does not hide his anguish. He says that his soul is sad to death. And he prays: "Do not be as I want, but as you will." Surrender is not an absence of struggle; it is a struggle that ends in the hands of the Father. He teaches us that it is possible to obey with tears.
questions: What "cup" are you asking God to remove?
Can you pray honestly and still say "thy will be done"?
days.application: Pray today with all sincerity about what troubles you, ending with "as you wish."

days.title: The gaze of Jesus
days.meditation: Peter denied it a third time, the rooster crowed, and Jesus turned and looked at him. Luke does not describe the look, but Peter left weeping bitterly. It must not have been a look of contempt; it was of wounded love. Sometimes, a look from Jesus breaks us more than any sermon, and this brokenness is the beginning of healing.
questions: When was the last time you felt Jesus' gaze on one of your failures?
Have you been avoiding that gaze or letting yourself be reached by it?
days.application: Confess to God today something you had been avoiding facing.

days.title: Father, forgive them
days.meditation: Preached to the cross, Jesus' first phrase was not about revenge, it was about forgiveness. He intercedes for those who crucified Him while they were still crucifying Him. Christ's forgiveness did not wait for the repentance of the guilty to be offered. It is this love that reaches us and challenges us to forgive.
questions: Who have you still not been able to forgive?
What does it change to know that Jesus forgave while still suffering?
days.application: Pray for the name of the person you need to forgive, even if the feeling hasn't changed yet.

days.title: It is consummated
days.meditation: A word in Greek, a world of meaning: tetelestai, "is paid." It is not the cry of the one who was defeated, but of the one who finished the work. Nothing needs to be added. Many Christians live as if they still owe installments of a paid debt. The cross says: it is finished.
questions: Do you still live as if you need to pay for something that Christ has already paid?
What would it be like to live today based on the accomplished work?
days.application: Write on a sheet the guilt you carry and, on top of that, "it's finished."

days.title: The Saturday of silence
days.meditation: Between Friday and Sunday there is a silent Sabbath. The body in the tomb, the rolled stone, the disciples hidden. The women watched where they laid him. Many times we live on this Sabbath: God seems silent, and hope seems buried. But God's silence is not the absence of God.
questions: Are you experiencing any "quiet Saturday" right now?
What helps you wait when God seems silent?
days.application: Write a prayer of waiting, telling God that you trust Him even in silence.

days.title: Why do you search among the dead?
days.meditation: The women went to the tomb with perfumes for a body. They found angels with a question: "Why do you seek among the dead the one who lives?" Sometimes we look for Jesus in the wrong place: in memories, in empty traditions, in defeat. He is not there. He has risen.
questions: In which "tomb" have you sought life?
What does the resurrection change in the way you will face this week?
days.application: Share with someone today, in a simple way, why the resurrection gives you hope.

plans.title: Christmas
plans.subtitle: The God who came to live nearby
plans.intro: Christmas is easy to decorate and hard to understand. This plan looks behind the lights at the mystery that changed history: the Eternal was born.

days.title: In the beginning
days.meditation: John begins Christmas ahead of time. Before the manger, there was the Word. Before the stars, it already existed. The baby of Bethlehem did not begin to exist there; he only entered the story he had created. It is as if the author of the book wrote himself as a character.
questions: What changes knowing that the Christmas baby is the Creator of everything?
Have you treated Jesus as a figure from the past or as the eternal Lord?
days.application: Read John 1:1-14 aloud, slowly, as a declaration of faith.

days.title: He emptied himself
days.meditation: Paul says that Christ did not cling to His equality with God, but emptied Himself. He did not cease to be God; He set aside privileges. Christmas is the greatest change of direction in history: from throne to stable. And Paul says: have that same mindset.
questions: Which privileges have you become too attached to?
Where can you "empty yourself" to serve someone this year-end?
days.application: Give up today something you are entitled to, for the good of another person.

days.title: A young woman from Nazareth
days.meditation: God sent an angel to a city of no importance, to an ordinary young woman, engaged to a carpenter. No palace. Heaven chooses addresses that the earth ignores. If God visited Nazareth, He can visit His street, His house, and His simplest routine.
questions: Do you think your life is too ordinary for God to visit?
What would it be like to wait for God in your routine this week?
days.application: During a common task today, pray: "Lord, visit this place."

days.title: José and the plan that changed
days.meditation: Joseph had a good and just plan: to keep Mary secret, without exposing her. Then God interrupted the plan with a dream. Sometimes our plans are not sinful, just small. Joseph's obedience cost him his reputation, but he put him at the center of the salvation story.
questions: What plan of yours, even if good, could God be trying to change?
What would you be willing to lose to obey?
days.application: Ask God in prayer if there is any plan of yours that needs to be delivered to Him.

days.title: Let's go to Belém
days.meditation: The shepherds listened and hurriedly went. They did not keep discussing the message in the field; they went to see. Faith that hears and does not go remains incomplete. Bethlehem is not just a place to remember, it is a place to go. Christmas invites you to leave the field and get close.
questions: Have you heard a lot about Jesus, but rarely come to him?
What concrete step would bring you closer to him this Christmas?
days.application: Set aside a moment just to worship Jesus, without requests, like the shepherds before the manger.

days.title: Where's the king?
days.meditation: The magi asked in Jerusalem: "Where is the king who was born?" The experts knew the answer, but they did not go. Herod knew too, and was frightened. It is possible to know the prophecies and remain still. Knowledge without seeking does not lead anyone to Bethlehem.
questions: You know a lot about Jesus but have searched little?
What has Christmas caused in you: curiosity, indifference, or adoration?
days.application: Choose a concrete way to seek Jesus this week beyond the usual.

days.title: He participated in flesh and blood
days.meditation: Hebrews explains why Christmas was necessary: Jesus became one of us to die for us and destroy the power of death. He did not save from afar. He entered our condition, our fatigue, our mortality. That is why he understands. And that is why he can free us from fear.
questions: What fear still enslaves you?
How does knowing that Jesus lived in our flesh change your prayer?
days.application: Tell Jesus today about a fear of yours, remembering that he knows human fragility from within.

days.title: In this, love was manifested
days.meditation: John defines love without romanticism: it was not we who loved God, but He loved us and sent His Son. Christmas is the visible proof of a love that took the initiative. We do not receive this gift, we receive it. And whoever receives this love learns to love in the same way.
questions: Do you live as someone who needs to win God's love or as someone who received it?
Who needs to see in you a love that takes the initiative?
days.application: Take the initiative today to love someone concretely: a visit, a gift, a request for forgiveness.
